podcast.title: Signed Aretha Franklin (1980)
podcast.body: In 1980, Arista Records signed Aretha Franklin, with Clive Davis spearheading an effort to reintroduce her as a contemporary pop star and modernize her sound. "The same year Franklin was on screen in the Blues Brothers. She signed a new recording contract with Arista Records."

podcast.title: Hired Andy Warhol for Album Art (1986)
podcast.body: In a "flex," Arista Records commissioned pop art legend Andy Warhol to paint the cover for Aretha Franklin's 1986 album *Aretha*, which became Warhol's last completed work before his death. "In a flex, Arista hired pop art legend Andy Warhol to paint the Aritha album cover."

podcast.title: Attempt to Make Graham Parker the "Next Bruce Springsteen"
podcast.body: Arista Records was "eager to make [Graham Parker] the next Bruce Springsteen" in the early 1980s. To achieve this, they connected Parker and The Rumour with producer Jimmy Iovine for the album "The Up Escalator," aiming for a more mainstream sound. "Arresta Records, eager to make him the next Bruce Springsteen, connected Parker and the rumor with producer Jimmy Iaveen."

podcast.title: Clive Davis's Role
podcast.body: Patti Smith publicly thanked Clive Davis, presumably of Arista Records, at her Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction, acknowledging his decision to give her a chance when she believed she had no talent. "On that night she thanked Clive Davis of Aresda for giving her a chance."

podcast.title: Clive Davis's Support
podcast.body: Clive Davis, the chief of Arista Records, provided Graham Parker with a substantial advance and a generous recording budget for what would become Parker's most celebrated album, 1979's *Squeezing Out Sparks*. "The label's chief Clive Davis gave Parker a big advance and an ample recording budget for what would turn out to be Parker's most celebrated album, 1979's Squeezing Out sparks."

podcast.title: Founded by Clive Davis (Mid-1970s)
podcast.body: Arista Records was launched in the mid-1970s by the influential music executive Clive Davis. "The label launched in the mid-70s by hard-charging music executive, Clive Davis."

podcast.title: Graham Parker's Label Switch
podcast.body: Graham Parker switched labels from Arista Records to Electra Records at some point after his 1983 single "Life Gets Better," indicating a search for a more suitable commercial home or artistic freedom. "after Parker switched labels again from Arista to Electra."

podcast.title: Graham Parker's New Label
podcast.body: Arista Records became Graham Parker's new label in the US after his departure from Mercury Records. "in the US by Parker's new label, Arista Records."

podcast.title: Signed Patti Smith Group
podcast.body: Arista Records signed the Patti Smith Group after their crucial seven-week residency at CBGB in spring 1975, which helped the band solidify their sound. "when those seven weeks were over they had a deal with eras to records."
